 Amazon's early Black Friday deals includes a fall-ready heavyweight Hanes hoodie for just $15 (plus 10 more fab deals)
 The cozy clothing clearance continues with $6 leggings, a $15 flannel and a pair of comfy Crocs for just $25.
 Chris McGraw Follow Editor, Deals Updated Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Updated Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.
 Hoodie weather is here to stay. (RealPeopleGroup via Getty Images) Once my spring and summer clothes are packed away, half my closet is fleece. We're talking zip-ups, pullovers in every color and brand you can think of. There's so much of it that the metal closet bar sags a few inches in the middle. That's how I know real fall has arrived, not the 80-degree "technically fall" days of late September.
 Another sure sign? Black Friday deals are showing up before I've even bought Halloween candy. Yes, it's early, nearly a month ahead of the big day, but retailers are already cutting prices and I'm not complaining. My favorite heavyweight hoodie , warm enough for the sidelines of a Saturday-morning soccer game without a jacket, is more than half off, just $15.
 Not a hoodie person? Don't let that stop you from perusing the best early Black Friday deals the internet has to offer today, with $6 bestselling leggings , $25 Crocs in a variety of colors and a $15 flannel rounding out the clothing in this list. 
 Our top deal of the day
 Amazon
 Hanes Ultimate Heavyweight Pullover Hoodie 
 $15 $33 Save $18 Why we love it: I've waxed poetic about the midweight Hanes EcoSmart hoodie — down as low as $10 right now , depending on the color — but when the blustery winds of late October start blowing, I find myself needing something a bit heavier. The Hanes Ultimate Hoodie is the brand's heaviest and, in my experience, warmest hoodie, and you can feel the difference the moment you put it on. It’s roughly 25% heavier than the EcoSmart, and it feels softer and breathes better too. That comes down to the fabric: a 9.7-oz. blend of 90% cotton and 10% polyester, compared with the EcoSmart’s 50/50 mix.
 Why we think it's a great deal: For just $15, you're getting a premium-feeling hoodie for nearly half off its already low MSRP. To go any heavier, you’ll need to step up to the Champion Reverse Weave (12-ounce) or the Carhartt Paxton (13-ounce) , which cost two and three times as much, respectively, and use less cotton.
 $15 at Amazon Explore More Buying Options $33 at Macy's 10 more deals to shop before they're gone
 Amazon
 Sinophant High-Waisted Leggings with Pockets 
 $6 $10 Save $4 Yeah, I did a double-take when I saw the price too — and the fact that these are Amazon's No. 1 bestselling leggings? Sold! The high waist stays put (no awkward roll-downs here), giving you smoothing tummy support without that can’t-breathe compression. The fabric is buttery soft with four-way stretch, so it moves with you, not against you. And the price? Just $6 for a classic black pair (styles vary) — which means these leggings are basically stretching your dollar in the best way possible.
 $6 at Amazon Amazon
 Yeti 16-ounce Travel Bottle 
 $24 $32 Save $8 Want your coffee to stay hot for hours? Yahoo's Britt Ross spoke with coffee experts, including Matt Scottoline of ReAnimator Coffee , who recommends a travel mug with double-wall vacuum insulation and a lid. This Yeti checks both boxes, keeping hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold. Its stainless steel construction resists rust and punctures, while the 360-degree lid lets you sip from any angle. Plus, it fits in a cupholder and is dishwasher-safe.
 Don't discount this 25%-off discount — it's the best we've seen on Amazon since this trail-ready tumbler's early-2026 debut. And with plenty of colors to choose from, good luck picking just one.
 $24 at Amazon Explore More Buying Options $24 at REI $32 at DICK'S Sporting Goods Walmart
 Sam's Club Plus and Walmart+ combined membership 
 $120/year $218/year Save $98 Walmart and Sam's Club just joined forces to give shoppers two annual memberships for the price of one. Sign up for Sam's Club Plus below, and you'll score a Walmart+ annual membership for no additional cost, along with your choice of a Paramount+ Essential or Peacock Premium annual subscription for free. Purchasing the memberships separately would cost $218, so you're saving nearly $100 by bundling.
 Great time to buy: Whether you're buying in bulk at Sam's or grabbing some essentials at Walmart, you'll be saving a whole lot right from the jump — Walmart+ alone would set you back $98 a year. And the savings keep coming once you make a few orders and recoup that membership fee in free shipping and delivery. Plus, you'll also score up to 2% Sam's Cash on all in-club qualifying purchases up to $750 a year. Oh, and you can even save 10¢ a gallon at participating gas stations .
 $120/year at Sam's Club Amazon
 Lego Disney Princess Advent Calendar 2026 
 $30 $45 Save $15 How about 24 days of tiny fairy-tale magic? There's Ariel, Cinderella, Moana and Mulan in microdoll form, plus sidekicks including Sebastian, Gus, Pua and Mushu — and honestly, the animal lineup alone is enough to win me over. There’s also a gingerbread castle, tiny piano, campfire and a spinning dance floor, because apparently the princesses are throwing quite the holiday party.
 Good deal : We've seen the Lego City and Star Wars Advent calendars sell out for 2026. While you can snag a few others, only this Disney Princess and the Lego Friends calendars are still on sale. If history is any indicator, this one will be gone before Thanksgiving, so scoop it up before it's back up to $45.
 $30 at Amazon Amazon
 Amazon Fire HD 10 tablet, 4GB RAM 
 $73 $155 Save $82 When I'm shopping for a new tablet, there are a few nonnegotiables, like lightweight design, long battery life, a generous screen and at least 64GB of storage (the sweet spot for most people). If you want something budget-friendly without skimping on quality, the Fire HD 10 checks all the boxes. It's already a steal compared to an iPad, but this deal makes the decision even more of a no-brainer.
 Good deal: If you've been holding out on upgrading your tablet, consider this a sign. This is over 50% off (and the lowest price we've ever seen). It's tough to find a tablet that packs this much punch at this price, so we recommend you stop waffling and buy.
 $73 at Amazon Explore More Buying Options $24 at REI $26 at DICK'S Sporting Goods Walmart
 Crocs Adult Baya Clogs 
 $25 $45 Save $20 Crocs are iconic for so many reasons: They're breathable, easy to slip on and obscenely comfortable. "They’re wide and extremely lightweight," says foot surgeon Dr. Diane Koshimune of these popular clogs. "People love to say that their favorite shoes are 'like walking on air,' but thousands of reviewers can confirm that in the case of Crocs, that is the total truth."
 We're not going to insist that you wear these with socks, but this color is very Santa- and Mrs. Claus-ready, if we do say so ourselves. Somehow these seem downright festive for the season ahead.
 $25 at Walmart Walmart
 Fantaslook Plaid Flannel Shirt 
 $15 $24 Save $9 Get ready for flannel season in style. This button-down has a slightly oversized fit and a curved hem to flatter a variety of shapes, and it's ideal for layering on warm days and chillier nights. Plus, it comes in 22 shades. Just note that it's not a thick flannel, but a lightweight layer that you can pair with a thermal when it's cooler out or a cami in warmer weather.
 It's got 17,000 five-star ratings, with one reviewer saying, "This shirt kept me looking good in cold weather. I also received many compliments on it. People were surprised I purchased it from Walmart!"
 Good deal : Nearly all of the 22 colors are on sale, but this pink shirt is the best deal at just $15.
 $15 at Walmart Amazon
 Apple AirTag (2nd Gen) 
 $23 $29 Save $6 Living 1,200 miles away from where I grew up means that the holiday season is also travel season. Pre-parenthood I never checked a bag, but with gifts and toys now in tow, that's no longer the case. Thanks to AirTags, I can track my bags from drop-off to the plane to the luggage carousel. And even when the worst happens, and my bags end up in Orlando when I'm in Michigan (true story), I know where they are and how to find them.
 "First, we bought one Apple AirTag for my husband's wallet. Then we bought a second one for his car keys," said this repeat buyer . "Now, we have a four-pack, which is cheaper, for our golf bags and checked roller bags."
 $23 at Amazon Explore More Buying Options $24 at Target $29 at Chewy Walmart
 Carote 14-Piece Knife Set with Wooden Block 
 $43 $80 Save $37 Trying to chop a slippery tomato with a dull knife is a headache, no matter how you slice it. Not only is it frustrating to use a blade that isn't sharp enough to pierce through the skin, it's also risky, as exerting more effort increases the likelihood of an accident. These days, just one decent knife can cost more than twice as much as this entire stainless steel set, so the fact that this collection comes with just about every type of knife a home cook could need makes it a steal at nearly half-off.
 $43 at Walmart Amazon
 Lisen Retractable Car Charger 
 $17 $20 Save $3 The average car on the road in the U.S. is over twelve years old, which means plenty of us are still working with limited or no built-in USB charging. Even if your car has one, a single port doesn't go far with multiple passengers. Most 12V cigarette lighter adapters solve this problem poorly: one outlet, cheap construction, easy to knock loose. The Lisen Retractable Car Charger addresses those issues: It has two retractable cables plus USB-C and USB-A ports, so you can charge up to four devices at once. 
 $17 at Amazon More shopping finds worth your time

 As October begins to wind down, so does Dyson Week , the brand's biggest sale of the year and your best chance to save up to 40% on vacuums, hair care products, air purifiers and more.

 Already worrying about what you're going to give that hard-to-buy-for guy in your life? Take it from someone who is that guy. My gift guide skips the stuff he'd buy himself and goes for the things he'll love but he'd never buy himself. It's sorted by price, from stocking stuffers under $10 to big-ticket splurges, with picks like a Stanley beer stein, a cast iron skillet he'll pass down someday and a Lego version of his dream car.
